0.35.0.lead: nexmail now connects with nextasks, nextime and nexpaper in one click, and attachments go straight into nexpaper. Also new: a list of your iPhones and iPads, AI tools (MCP), one AI provider for everybody, backups in one list, and settings that look like those of every nex app.

sections.title: Connect other nex apps in one click
sections.body: Instead of making an API key in the other app and typing it in here, you click Connect with nextasks, Connect with nextime or Connect with nexpaper; each app has a card of its own. The other app opens and shows who you are signed in as and what each app gets from the other, in plain words such as “Create and change tasks”. Agree once and you are back here. Each connection may do only what it needs: in nextasks you pick the spaces, in nexpaper the vaults. The card shows since when you are connected, when the connection was last used and what it may do, with Renew and Disconnect, which ends both sides. If the other app cannot be reached right now, the card offers Check now, and if something goes wrong, the reason is in the card.

sections.title: nextasks and nextime: now connected in one click
sections.body: What you know from nextasks and nextime now works without a key. Turn into task makes a task in a nextasks list from a mail. The lists stand in the sidebar of the tasks, where you tick off, change date and priority and pick who is responsible. The calendars of nextime show in nexmail's calendar: you create, change and delete events there, accept an invitation straight into a nextime calendar, and Turn into event makes an event from any mail. Connections made with a key keep working, and the card lets you renew them the new way.

sections.title: Attachments straight to nexpaper
sections.where: Reading pane, next to each attachment
sections.body: New: with nexpaper connected, every attachment of a message has Send to nexpaper as a document next to it. One click puts the file into nexpaper's inbox, a bill or a contract for example. If nexmail may store into more than one vault, a small window asks which one; the one you used last is chosen.

sections.title: iPhone and iPad in one place
sections.body: All paired iPhones and iPads now stand in the card Devices at the top, with when each was last seen and whether it gets notifications. You rename a device, disconnect it or disconnect them all at once. Connect iPhone or iPad shows a QR code as before, with a code to type below it. When a new device comes in, you get the mail about a new sign-in as for a new browser, if Mail me about a new sign-in is on. The iPhone app itself does not change with this update: it connects as before, and every device already paired keeps working without pairing again.

sections.title: Notifications per device
sections.body: Under Notifications on your devices you choose for each iPhone and iPad whether it tells you about new mail and event reminders. Which way says how many devices are connected and on how many notifications are allowed. The list also has “New device connected” and, for operators, “New version of nexmail”; a coming version of the iPhone app will be the first to show these two.

sections.title: For the operator: Server › Connections
sections.body: Everything that connects nexmail with other programs now has a page of its own, the counterpart of My account › Connections. In Other nex apps you enter the address of nextasks, nextime and nexpaper once, and from then on every account connects in one click. If an app is not set up yet, the card says so, and shows you a link to this place. If one of the apps runs in your own network (LAN, VPN), allow it with Connections into the local network; the switch at the top turns connections off altogether, existing ones then rest, and nothing is deleted. In Interfaces you switch the API for members, the AI tools (MCP) and the iPhone app on or off.

sections.title: AI tools (MCP)
sections.body: An AI program such as Claude Code can now work with your mail: count unread messages, search and read mail, draft replies, set tags, move messages and tick off tasks. It sees only the mailboxes you give it and never sends anything; drafts land in the Drafts folder. It reads the text of a mail only with the extra Read mail text. For each tool you choose Allow, Ask or Deny; a question shows up in your browser. Off by default: the operator switches it on under Server › Connections › Interfaces.

sections.title: One AI provider for everybody
sections.where: Server › AI provider; My account › AI
sections.body: As the operator you can now set up one AI service for all accounts instead of everybody entering their own, and set how often it may be asked. Besides the OpenAI form, nexmail now also speaks Anthropic's Messages form. Own accesses reach computers in your own network only once you list them; a computer already in use is on the list by itself after the update. Under My account › AI everybody sees where their texts go, can switch the AI off for themselves and finds word for word what went out. An existing installation stays with Each account itself.

sections.title: Backups in one list
sections.body: All backups now stand in one list, whether scheduled, made by hand or made before an update. The schedule runs at a time of day you pick, monthly too if you like. Back up now asks for a note. A download is an encrypted file with a password of its own; after the password it tells when it was made, what kind it is and its note. Before a restore nexmail makes a copy, and the window asks whether the public address from the backup should apply.

sections.title: Managing accounts
sections.body: There can now be several operators. You block an account and unblock it; while it is blocked, nexmail fetches no mail for it and sends it no notifications. A deleted account can be brought back for 30 days, and deleting asks for your own password. Paired iPhones and iPads rest while an account is blocked or deleted and work again afterwards without pairing anew; only deleting for good disconnects them. Under Manage you see how many devices an account has, of which kind and when last seen, never their names, disconnect them with Disconnect devices, and set whether the account may use the AI.

sections.title: Settings like in every nex app
sections.where: Bottom of the sidebar: name · Settings
sections.body: The settings now have the same layout, buttons and windows as the other nex apps. Dates and times look the same everywhere and follow your account's time zone. Light, Dark or As the system now belongs to your account and applies on every device; new accounts start with As the system. Older links to a settings page still lead to the right place.

small: Languages of your own: under Server › General › Languages the operator adds more languages as a JSON file. A template to translate can be downloaded there, and missing texts fall back to English.
The log under Server › Log looks like in the other nex apps and can be downloaded as text.

Only the operator looks for new versions; members see their version and nothing of the check. The setup asks once whether nexmail may look. In the background nexmail looks at most once a day, and only while Check once a day is on and a device of an operator wants notices of new versions; that device then hears of each new version once.
An iPhone or iPad not used for a year is disconnected by nexmail on its own.
A context menu is never taller than the window, and a submenu stays wholly visible.
Without a public https address, the Passkeys box says what is missing instead of showing a button that cannot work.

After the update everything keeps working: connections made with a key, API keys, paired iPhones and your AI settings. New tables are added on start, and nexmail makes a backup first; nothing is renamed or removed.
The interface's addresses of before (/api/v1, /api/protokoll, /api/sicherung, /api/ueber) answer as they did.

0.34.0.lead: Signing in, your profile and security are rebuilt: sign in with your username or email, passkeys, two ways back from a forgotten password, and system mails that try again after an error. The way you sign in today keeps working.

sections.title: Sign in with username or email
sections.body: You sign in with your username or your account's email address. “Stay signed in” is on by default; without the tick, the sign-in ends when you close the browser. When a sign-in runs out, you sign in again in a window on top, and the open page stays where it was.

sections.title: Change your name, username and address
sections.body: You change your display name, username and email yourself and save them with one button; for the username and the address nexmail asks for your password. With an outgoing mail server, a new address counts once you have opened the link in the confirmation mail. Your language now belongs to the account and applies on every device. Without a profile picture, a letter on a colour stands in.

sections.title: Forgot your password
sections.body: You ask for a link to a new password with your username or email; it goes to your account's address and lasts one hour. If that is not possible, the operator makes a link under “Accounts” and sends it by mail or passes it on to you. A new password signs out every browser; afterwards nexmail shows which devices still have access and disconnects them if you want.

sections.title: Passkeys and second factor
sections.body: Password, second factor, passkeys and signed-in devices now each have a box of their own. With a passkey you sign in without password or code (over https only). You make new recovery codes there yourself. When somebody signs in from a browser nexmail does not know yet, you get a mail; you can switch that off.

sections.title: Invitations without a set name
sections.body: An invitation needs only an email address and a name, both optional, and you choose how long the link lasts (1, 7 or 30 days). The person invited picks their own username. Without an outgoing mail server of its own, nexmail shows the link for you to pass on.

sections.title: For the operator
sections.where: Server › Sign-in, Server › Accounts and Server › Mail
sections.body: Under “Sign-in” you can require a second factor of everybody and switch passkeys off. If somebody lost their phone, you reset their second factor under “Accounts”. nexmail tries system mails again later after an error; under “Mail” you see the last mail sent, the last error and what is still waiting.

small: Everything keeps working after the update: sign-ins, passwords, second factors, paired iPhones and API keys. New passwords need at least 12 characters; older, shorter ones stay valid.
Only a new server without any account asks for a setup code. It is in the log (“docker logs nexmail”) or comes from NEXMAIL_SETUP_TOKEN; a running installation never asks for it.
NEXMAIL_ZWEI_FAKTOR_AUS still works; NEXMAIL_SECOND_FACTOR_OFF is the same switch under a second name.
After ten wrong passwords an account is locked for 15 minutes; a browser you have signed in with before is exempt.
Every signed-in account now sees profile pictures, not only you and the operator.
“Kennwort” is now called “Passwort” everywhere in German.

0.33.0.lead: nexmail now works with nextime and nextasks: all calendars through one connection, tasks from nextasks right in nexmail. Plus symbols for your mailboxes and the appearance “Like the system”.

sections.title: Connect nextime
sections.body: Instead of adding each calendar on its own, you connect nextime once with its address and key. All calendars show up in nexmail's calendar, in nextime's groups and colours; you tick in the card which ones nexmail uses. You change, add and delete events right there. “Add calendar” lists nextime first.

sections.title: Invitations and events from mails
sections.body: Accept an invitation in one step and pick the calendar while you do; nexmail remembers per mailbox which one you used last. The card says whether the event is already in nextime and what overlaps it. “Turn into event” makes an event from any mail.

sections.title: nextasks right in Tasks
sections.body: With nextasks connected, its spaces and lists appear in the sidebar with their symbols. Tick tasks off, change date, time, priority and assignees, add new tasks, also without a mail, and search them. You pick in the card which lists nexmail shows. nexmail's own task list can be switched off; its open tasks can move to your default list when you do.

sections.title: Colour and symbol for mailboxes
sections.body: Each mailbox can get a symbol and a colour as in nextasks, an own colour too. The symbol then shows wherever the coloured dot was. Without a symbol the dot stays.

sections.title: Light, dark or like the system
sections.body: With “Like the system”, nexmail follows your device's setting and switches with it.

small: The nextime and nextasks cards under “Connections” are laid out as in nextime: the state at the top, the sections below, “Change key” and “Disconnect” at the bottom.
There is only one nextasks connection now; others from before stay in the card with a note.

0.24.0.lead: From this version on, nexmail tells you after an update what has changed. This text is the first one.

sections.title: What's new, right after the update
sections.where: Banner below the top bar, later under About nexmail › What's new
sections.body: When an update brings something new, a banner shows at the top. One click opens this text, the cross puts the banner away. It is remembered per account on the server, so on all your devices at once.

small: Large Gmail folders sync completely. Before, they stopped at 1000 messages.
Mailboxes connected through Google or Microsoft can send again.
A mailbox can be switched between a password and a consent.
If the browser refuses to register for notifications, the page now says why, and names browsers without Google's push service, such as Helium.
Very large mailboxes no longer break off the sync.

0.24.5.lead: A page the browser translated no longer takes nexmail down.

sections.title: Pages the browser translated
sections.where: Every page, when Chrome, Edge or an extension translates it
sections.body: A translated page could go blank as soon as something on it changed, because the browser had swapped the texts for its own. nexmail now keeps working on such a page.

0.25.0.lead: One-click unsubscribe, AI help for mail you receive, a command palette, and new mail now shows up by itself.

sections.title: Unsubscribe from newsletters
sections.where: Reading pane, the “Unsubscribe” button on mail from a list
sections.body: When a mail offers a way out, a button is there. If the sender is verified, nexmail does it for you, otherwise the unsubscribe page or a prepared mail opens. nexmail asks first and names the other side. The button shows on mail you open for the first time after the update.

sections.title: AI for mail you receive
sections.where: My account › AI, switch “My received mail”, then in the reading pane and when replying
sections.body: With an AI service set up, nexmail summarises a mail, translates it, answers a question about it or drafts a reply. This is off by default because the mail goes to your service, and the operator has to allow it as well. All AI settings now live on the AI page.

sections.title: Everything from one key
sections.body: A search field finds folders, sections and the actions for the open mail, without touching the mouse.

sections.title: New mail shows up by itself
sections.where: The message list, and per mailbox the switch “See new mail right away”
sections.body: An open window now loads new mail by itself. “See new mail right away” is faster still. It keeps a second connection to the mail server open and is therefore off by default.

sections.title: Drop attachments
sections.body: Files can be dragged straight into the window. Pictures you drag into the text land at that very spot.

sections.title: Selections across mailboxes
sections.where: All inboxes and the folder column
sections.body: Delete, archive and move now work when a selection spans several mailboxes. Each mail goes to the trash or archive of its own mailbox, and undo brings them all back. Dragging into another mailbox works too.

small: Replies to invitations and out-of-office notes now go out right away. Before, they waited for the next restart.
Opening a mail no longer tears its conversation apart. Conversations that were split grow back together after the update.
Fast typing no longer loses characters, and Escape no longer throws away what you typed.
Highlighting and font size now reach the recipient.
An attachment that is still being read blocks sending instead of quietly dropping out.
Rules can add a tag.
Newsletters no longer show CSS in the message list.
nexmail is ready for an iPhone app, which pairs under “Connect iPhone”.

0.26.0.lead: Tasks from mail can now go to Todoist, and what you complete there, nexmail sees too.

sections.title: Connect Todoist
sections.body: Paste the API token from Todoist. nexmail checks it and keeps it encrypted. It is yours alone, everyone connects their own app. This is also where you pick the default list: your Todoist list, or nexmail's own list as before.

sections.title: List and due date when you create it
sections.body: With a connection, nexmail asks briefly: title, list and due date, with Today, Tomorrow and Next week one tap away. Only the title, the date, the sender and a link back to the mail go to Todoist, never the text of the mail. If a mail already has a task, nexmail says where instead of making a second one.

sections.title: Done in both directions
sections.body: Tick a task in nexmail and Todoist knows right away. Complete, reschedule or delete it in Todoist and nexmail follows a few minutes later, or at once when you open the task list. The date of a Todoist task is changed in Todoist.

small: Removing a Todoist task takes it out of nexmail only, it stays in Todoist.
Tasks created directly in Todoist do not show up in nexmail. The list stays the list of your mail.

0.27.0.lead: Tasks from mail can now also go to a tool of your own, through a webhook.

sections.title: Connect a webhook
sections.body: Next to Todoist there is now “Connect a webhook”. nexmail sends every task as JSON to your address, signed with a secret that is shown only once. The address is saved only after it answers a probe; “Send test” checks it again later and names the status if something is wrong.

sections.title: Send only, or report back
sections.where: My account › Connections › Tasks and My account › Connections › API keys
sections.body: With “Send only”, nexmail does not keep the task in its own list, because it gets done in the other tool. Or the tool reports back: an API key with “May tick off tasks” completes and reopens tasks through the API.

sections.title: Message text only when allowed
sections.where: Server › General › Features for every account
sections.body: A webhook can include the text of the message if its user turns it on and the operator allows it. It is off by default. Addresses on the local network work, as with calendars, only once the operator allows them.

small: For a webhook, localhost gets its own hint: inside the container it is nexmail itself, what you want is the host's address on your network.
Tick a webhook task in nexmail and the tool hears about it right away.

0.28.0.lead: A tool that gets tasks through the webhook can now also tag the message.

sections.title: Tags through the API
sections.body: An API key can now have “May tag messages”. With it, another tool adds a tag to the message of a task and removes it again, for example “Done” when the task is ticked off there. The tag goes to the mail server, just as when you set it yourself, so it also shows up in Thunderbird and on your phone. The option is separate from ticking off tasks.

sections.title: Tags in the webhook
sections.body: Every task event now lists the tags on the message, with their ID and name. The other tool knows right away how the message is tagged here.

small: If the same message sits in several folders of a mailbox, every copy gets the tag.
When a tool changes a tag through the API, nothing is sent back to the webhook.

0.29.0.lead: Tasks from messages can now go to nextasks, the self-hosted to-do app from the same family.

sections.title: nextasks as a to-do app
sections.body: Enter the address of your nextasks and an API token that may “Read and write”. Then “Turn into task” lets you pick a list, with its space and section. As with Todoist: one message, one task, even if you turn it into a task twice. What goes out is the title, the date, the sender and a link back to the message, never the message text.

sections.title: nextasks owns the tick
sections.body: What you tick off in nexmail is ticked off in nextasks. What is completed, reopened, rescheduled or put in the bin in nextasks shows up in nexmail a few minutes later. A repeating task stays open after you tick it off and shows its next date right away.

small: When the token runs out, enter a new one under “Renew token”; your tasks stay connected.
If nextasks is on your local network, the operator has to allow that under Administration → Servers, as for webhooks and calendars.

0.30.0.lead: nexmail has a new icon: an envelope.

sections.title: New icon
sections.body: The mark is now an envelope with a darker green frame. The logo follows light and dark mode, the browser tab follows your system and now shows the envelope instead of the nexapps mark. The icons for the home screen and the logo in system mails are new as well.
sections.where: Header, sign-in, browser tab, home screen and system mails

small: The browser now asks before it uses icons, the manifest and the service worker again, so a new icon reaches an installed web app too.
The database does not change.

0.31.0.lead: The settings are reorganised, deleted mail disappears at once, and mailbox groups sit as tabs above the list.

sections.title: One settings page for everything
sections.where: Bottom of the sidebar: name · Settings
sections.body: Your account is at the top left, then “My account”, “Mail” and, for the operator, “Server”, with “About nexmail” at the end. Administration, the AI page and the About page are no longer entries of their own in the rail but sections in there. Administration is now “Server”, to-do apps, the iPhone app and API keys are under “Connections”, and AI is under “Mail”. Everyone can see “About nexmail” now.

sections.title: Profile with picture and name
sections.body: You can upload a profile picture and change your name. The email address for account matters is here now instead of under Security, along with the language and “Sign out”. Light and dark are under “Appearance”; the two switches at the top right are gone.

sections.title: Deleting without waiting
sections.where: Message list: Delete, E, Move and swipe
sections.body: A deleted, archived or moved message disappears at once, and “Undo” shows at the same moment. The server keeps working behind it. If it refuses, the message comes back and the notice says why. The undo bar is green now and easy to see on a light list.

sections.title: Mailbox groups as tabs
sections.where: Above the folder column and the list
sections.body: The tags of your mailboxes, such as “private” and “work”, sit as tabs right above what they filter, with the number of unread messages. Before, they were small buttons at the top of the folder column.

sections.title: Ctrl+A selects all
sections.body: Ctrl+A, Cmd+A on a Mac, selects all loaded messages in the list. Delete, E and the context menu then act on all of them. In the search field and in an open message, Ctrl+A selects text as usual.

small: If the connection drops while the folder list is read, the sync carries on with the folders it knows instead of skipping that mailbox. The log no longer reports this as an error.
The wordmark at the top left is the same as in the other nex apps.
On start, two columns for the profile picture are added. Going back to 0.30 works as is.

0.31.1.lead: Polish for 0.31.0: mailbox groups can be put in order, switches look like in the other nex apps, and unsaved changes no longer get lost silently.

sections.title: Order the tabs yourself
sections.where: Mailbox groups above the folder column and the list
sections.body: Drag a tab to where you want it. The order is stored with your account and applies on all your devices. “All” stays first.

sections.title: Switches as ticks
sections.body: Ticks replace the sliding switches, as in nexnotes and nextasks: name and explanation on the left, the tick on the right. Where a card already says what it is about, only the tick stands on the right.

sections.title: Asked before discarding
sections.body: If you changed something in the mailbox window and did not save it, nexmail asks before closing, whether by the cross, Escape or a click beside it.

small: A subtle line separates the favourites from the mailboxes.
On start, a column for the order of the tabs is added.

0.32.0.lead: nexmail now looks and works like nexnotes and nextasks: no more rail on the left, the views at the top, and your settings at the bottom of the sidebar.

sections.title: The views are at the top
sections.body: Mail, Calendar, Tasks and Contacts are buttons in the toolbar, right after the sidebar button. Next to them are the view's main action, “New message”, “New event” or “New contact”, and the search. The narrow rail on the far left is gone and gives its space to the list.

sections.title: Your profile at the bottom of the sidebar
sections.where: Bottom of the sidebar: name · Settings
sections.body: One click opens the settings at your profile, beside the sidebar of the view you came from. The menu at the top right is gone: “What's new” is under “About nexmail”, the second factor under “Security”, “Sign out” in the profile. Add a mailbox under “Mailboxes”.

sections.title: Sidebars for calendar, contacts and tasks
sections.body: All three now have a sidebar like the mail folders: collapsible, resizable, with your profile at the bottom. In Contacts it holds address books and groups, with the contact list next to it. Tasks can be filtered by “Open”, “Today and overdue”, “With date” and “Done” and, with a connected to-do app, by where they live.

sections.title: Calendars and address books in the settings
sections.where: My account › Calendars and address books
sections.body: Add, rename and disconnect calendars, connect and disconnect address books, all in one place. The calendar itself has a “+” next to the “Calendars” heading for the same.

sections.title: Ctrl+K jumps to the search
sections.body: As in the other nex apps, Ctrl+K, Cmd+K on a Mac, takes you to the search field; Ctrl+F still works. The command palette with every action now opens with Ctrl+Shift+P.

small: The mailbox group tabs and the search fields look as they do in nexnotes.
nexmail now uses the Inter typeface throughout, like the other nex apps.
The notice about blocked images has its text on top and “Load images” and “Always load” below.
